audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for no condemnation, Spirit of life, mind of flesh/Spirit, adoption, creation groaning, Spirit intercession, conformed to Son, inseparable love.

verses.restored: There is therefore now no condemnation for those in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

modern.text: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

original.text: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ·

verses.restored: For the law/principle of the Spirit of life in Messiah Jesus released you from the law/principle of sin/misalignment and death.

familiar.text: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death.

modern.text: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν ⸀σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.

verses.restored: For the impossible thing of the Law, in which it was weak through flesh, the Divine did: sending his own Son in likeness of flesh of sin/misalignment and concerning sin/misalignment, he condemned sin/misalignment in the flesh,

familiar.text: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:

modern.text: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh,

original.text: τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί,

verses.restored: so that the righteous/just requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to flesh but according to Spirit.

familiar.text: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

modern.text: so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

original.text: ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα·

verses.restored: For those being according to flesh set their mind on the things of flesh; but those according to Spirit, the things of Spirit.

familiar.text: For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

modern.text: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

original.text: οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.

verses.restored: For the mind of flesh is death, but the mind of Spirit is life and peace.

familiar.text: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.

modern.text: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,

original.text: τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη·

verses.restored: Because the mind of flesh is hostility toward the Divine, for it does not submit to the Law of the Divine, for it is not able.

familiar.text: Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.

modern.text: because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.

original.text: διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν, τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται, οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται·

verses.restored: Those being in flesh are not able to please the Divine.

familiar.text: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

modern.text: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.

verses.restored: But you are not in flesh but in Spirit, if indeed Spirit of the Divine dwells in you. If anyone does not have Spirit of Messiah, this one is not his.

familiar.text: But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

modern.text: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.

original.text: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν. εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: But if Messiah is in you, the body indeed is dead because of sin/misalignment, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.

modern.text: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.

original.text: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην.

verses.restored: If the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, the One who raised Messiah from the dead will also make alive your mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in you.

familiar.text: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

modern.text: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you. Heirs with Christ

original.text: εἰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος ⸀τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὁ ἐγείρας ⸂ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃ ζῳοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ ⸂τὸ ἐνοικοῦν αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: So then, siblings, we are debtors, not to flesh, to live according to flesh.

familiar.text: Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.

modern.text: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.

original.text: Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν, οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν,

verses.restored: For if you live according to flesh, you are about to die; but if by Spirit you put to death the practices of the body, you will live.

familiar.text: For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.

modern.text: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνῄσκειν, εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε, ζήσεσθε.

verses.restored: For as many as are led by Spirit of the Divine, these are sons/children of the Divine.

familiar.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

modern.text: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.

original.text: ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι ⸂υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ⸃.

verses.restored: For you did not receive spirit of slavery again into fear, but you received Spirit of adoption, in whom we cry, Abba, Father.

familiar.text: For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.

modern.text: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ·

verses.restored: The Spirit itself bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of the Divine.

familiar.text: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:

modern.text: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.

original.text: αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.

verses.restored: And if children, also heirs: heirs of the Divine and co-heirs with Messiah, if indeed we suffer together so that we may also be glorified together.

familiar.text: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

modern.text: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him. Future Glory (2 Corinthians 5:1–10)

original.text: εἰ δὲ τέκνα, καὶ κληρονόμοι· κληρονόμοι μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ, εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν.

verses.restored: For I calculate that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy compared with the glory about to be unveiled into us.

familiar.text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.

modern.text: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.

original.text: Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.

verses.restored: For the eager expectation of creation awaits the unveiling of the sons/children of the Divine.

familiar.text: For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.

modern.text: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.

original.text: ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται·

verses.restored: For creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the One who subjected it, upon hope,

familiar.text: For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope,

modern.text: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope

original.text: τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη, οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα, ⸀ἐφʼ ἑλπίδι

verses.restored: that creation itself also will be released from the slavery of decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of the Divine.

familiar.text: Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.

modern.text: that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.

original.text: ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For we know that all creation groans together and suffers birth pains together until now.

familiar.text: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

modern.text: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.

original.text: οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συστενάζει καὶ συνωδίνει ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν·

verses.restored: And not only this, but we ourselves, having the firstfruit of the Spirit, also groan within ourselves, awaiting adoption, the redemption/release of our body.

familiar.text: And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.

modern.text: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.

original.text: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ ⸂καὶ αὐτοὶ⸃ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἔχοντες ⸂ἡμεῖς καὶ⸃ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς στενάζομεν, υἱοθεσίαν ἀπεκδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν.

verses.restored: For in hope we were saved/healed; but hope being seen is not hope. For who hopes for what one sees?

familiar.text: For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?

modern.text: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?

original.text: τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν· ἐλπὶς δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς, ὃ γὰρ βλέπει ⸀τίς ἐλπίζει;

verses.restored: But if we hope for what we do not see, through endurance we await it.

familiar.text: But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

modern.text: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.

original.text: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ βλέπομεν ἐλπίζομεν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.

verses.restored: Likewise also the Spirit helps together with our weakness; for what we should pray as is necessary, we do not know, but the Spirit itself intercedes with unspeakable groanings.

familiar.text: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

modern.text: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.

original.text: Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα συναντιλαμβάνεται ⸂τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ⸃ ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ τί ⸀προσευξώμεθα καθὸ δεῖ οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἀλλὰ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ⸀ὑπερεντυγχάνει στεναγμοῖς ἀλαλήτοις,

verses.restored: The One searching hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because according to the Divine, it intercedes for holy ones.

familiar.text: And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.

modern.text: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God. God Works in All Things (Ephesians 1:3–14)

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἐραυνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων.

verses.restored: We know that for those loving the Divine, all things work together into good, for those called according to purpose.

familiar.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

modern.text: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.

original.text: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι τὸν θεὸν πάντα ⸀συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν, τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν.

verses.restored: Because those whom he foreknew, he also marked out beforehand to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be firstborn among many siblings.

familiar.text: For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

modern.text: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.

original.text: ὅτι οὓς προέγνω, καὶ προώρισεν συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πρωτότοκον ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς·

verses.restored: Those whom he marked out beforehand, these he also called; and those whom he called, these he also made righteous/just; and those whom he made righteous/just, these he also glorified.

familiar.text: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

modern.text: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.

original.text: οὓς δὲ προώρισεν, τούτους καὶ ἐκάλεσεν· καὶ οὓς ἐκάλεσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδικαίωσεν· οὓς δὲ ἐδικαίωσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδόξασεν.

verses.restored: What then shall we say to these things? If the Divine is for us, who is against us?

familiar.text: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?

modern.text: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?

original.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα; εἰ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τίς καθʼ ἡμῶν;

verses.restored: He who did not spare his own Son but handed him over for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?

familiar.text: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?

modern.text: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?

original.text: ὅς γε τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πάντων παρέδωκεν αὐτόν, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαρίσεται;

verses.restored: Who will bring accusation against the chosen ones of the Divine? The Divine is the one making righteous/just.

familiar.text: Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God’s elect? It is God that justifieth.

modern.text: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.

original.text: τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ; θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν·

verses.restored: Who is the one condemning? Messiah Jesus is the one who died, rather was raised, who is also at the right hand of the Divine, who also intercedes for us.

familiar.text: Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

modern.text: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God—and He is interceding for us. More than Conquerors (Psalms 44:1–26)

original.text: τίς ὁ ⸀κατακρινῶν; ⸀Χριστὸς ὁ ἀποθανών, μᾶλλον ⸀δὲ ⸀ἐγερθείς, ὅς ⸀καί ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: Who will separate us from the love of Messiah? Pressure, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, or sword?

familiar.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

modern.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?

original.text: τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ; θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα;

verses.restored: Just as it is written: Because of you we are being put to death the whole day; we were counted as sheep of slaughter.

familiar.text: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

modern.text: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”

original.text: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς.

verses.restored: But in all these things we more than conquer through the One who loved us.

familiar.text: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.

modern.text: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.

verses.restored: For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, neither messengers nor rulers, neither present things nor coming things, nor powers,

familiar.text: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,

modern.text: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,

original.text: πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ οὔτε ⸂ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα οὔτε δυνάμεις⸃

verses.restored: neither height nor depth, nor any other creature, will be able to separate us from the love of the Divine in Messiah Jesus our Lord.

familiar.text: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

modern.text: neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

original.text: οὔτε ὕψωμα οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.

translation_notes: Flesh in Romans 8 refers to a domination-pattern opposed to Spirit, not the body as evil. Verse 11 explicitly includes mortal bodies being made alive.
Creation groaning is cosmic liberation language and should be kept ecological/embodied, not reduced to private spirituality.
